record.title: Is there a CRT-style result for Approximate GCD?
record.statement:
Is there a CRT-style result for Approximate GCD? 

In particular, given X as a product of distinct primes, can we find any of the primes if we are allowed a polynomial number of sample numbers n so that n is small mod p for each of the primes?

record.title: The Chowla conjecture implies that … cannot be orthogonal to all uniquely ergodic systems (allowing non-zero entropy).

record.title: Relative conductor of $p$-adic groups
record.statement:
Let $H \leq G$ be groups over $\mathbb{Q}_p$, $\pi$ be an admissible representation of $G$, and $K_G$ be a maximal compact of $G$. Define

$$
K_H(p^n):= \{g \in K_G \mid (g \mod p^n) \in H\}.
$$

Does $\pi$ have a non-zero vector fixed by $K_H(p^n)$ for some $n$?

If so, what's the smallest such $n$?
record.source_name: AimPL: Analytic, arithmetic, and geometric aspects of automorphic forms (posed by Mladen Dimitrov)

record.title: Meta problem about values & derivatives
record.statement:
Given a subconvexity result

$$
L(\pi, \frac{1}{2}) \ll c(\pi)^{\frac{1}{4} - \delta};
$$

1) find an analogue of the result where the size of $L(\pi, \frac{1}{2})$ is replaced by some "arithmetic" analogue of size, or

2) find an analogue of the result for the derivative $L'(\pi, \frac{1}{2})$.

record.title: Regularity of free boundary/obstacle problem
record.statement:
Consider the following Cauchy problem, 

$$
\begin{cases}
\max\{\partial_tu + v\cdot \nabla_xu - \mathscr{L}_vu, u - \varphi\} = 0\\
u(0) = u_0.
\end{cases}
$$

Determine the regularity of solutions for $\mathscr{L} = \nabla_v^s$ (This is known in $d = 1$)

Determine the regularity of solutions of the free boundary: $\{u = \varphi\}$
record.source_name: AimPL: Integro-differential equations in many-particle interacting systems

record.title: Alt-Caffarelli type problem
record.statement:
Find a function that satisfies the Kolmogorov equation

$$
\begin{cases}
(\partial_t + v\cdot \nabla_x - \Delta_v)f = 0, & f > 0\\
|\nabla_vf| = 1, & \partial\{f > 0\}.
\end{cases}
$$

Derive and study the reasonable Alt-Caffarelli type problem.
